typescript.x-note: Any value reference to the global counts, not only calls: aliases, destructuring, bracket access and globalThis reach the same source. Bun, Deno and fetch are globals with effects that no banned import can see. Math, crypto, import.meta and the global objects are allowed only as the object of a member access to something else (Math.max, crypto.subtle, import.meta.url); a global object reached through another one (globalThis.window) is the global again. Type positions are type_identifier and never match; the namespace of a qualified type (Temporal.Instant) is an identifier and is skipped. A name the file binds is not the global: not-the-global walks the enclosing scopes outward and, in each, looks for a parameter, variable, destructured name, function, class, non-const enum or import from a relative module bound there without entering nested scopes, so a parameter named window in one function leaves the global window in another reported. A declare, a type-only import, a parameter of a function type, a namespace or const enum (either may emit no value), a for-of or for-in target without const, let or var (it assigns the global) and an import from a package or builtin (randomInt from node:crypto) bind nothing that replaces the effect; a var hoisted out of a nested block is not seen (a false deny, the safe direction). params.allow lists qualified references the project declares pure (Bun.Glob, Bun.JSONC): a match is dropped when the member chain it heads starts with an entry (new Bun.Glob(x)); the bare global, an alias, destructuring, bracket access and a longer name (Bun.Globber) stay denied.
